evals.prompt: We expect 10M daily active users, each reading their feed 20 times a day. How much traffic is that and what does it mean for the design?
evals.expected_output: Computes average QPS from DAU and actions per day, applies a peak factor, compares to a single-node ceiling, and names the shaping quantity that dictates the first component.

value: DAU x actions per user per day / 86,400
assertions.description: Uses the QPS formula rather than a guess
Connects the number to a design consequence

evals.prompt: Our API calls three services in sequence, each 99.9% available, with one cross-region hop. Can we promise 99.9% and 200ms p95?
evals.expected_output: Shows that serial dependencies multiply so three 99.9% services yield a composite below target, sums the latency budget including the cross-region round trip, and converts the target into an error budget while budgeting with p99 rather than the mean.

assertions.description: Applies availability math to a serial chain
Builds a latency budget from hop costs
Converts the target into an operational budget

evals.prompt: How much storage will we need for 20M posts a day at 1KB each, kept for a year with 3x replication?
evals.expected_output: Applies the storage formula including retention and replication factor, will round every input to one significant figure rather than report unverified precision, and restates each assumed input beside the result.

assertions.description: Includes retention and replication in the projection

value: Round every input to one significant figure

should_trigger: Give me a back of envelope estimate for this service
What peak QPS should we provision for?
How much storage will this feature need in a year?
What is our latency budget across these hops?
should_not_trigger: Write a unit test for the pricing helper
Explain what a pointer is in Go

pressure_scenarios.prompt: We have no traffic numbers and nobody will get them today. Just assume web-scale and tell me the infrastructure we need to buy.

rationalizations: Nobody can get the numbers today, just assume web-scale.
Give me a precise figure so I can put it in the budget.
Round numbers look unprofessional in a plan.
red_flags: Reporting a precise figure derived from an invented input.
Provisioning from an average with no peak factor stated.
Omitting the assumed inputs beside the result.
